question: Which point-in-time variables and feature families explain the predictive advantage of the T2 engaged head?
hypothesis: Accumulated interaction history and current lead-to-spot context explain more of T2 ranking power than static lead intake fields alone.
primary_change: out-of-sample permutation importance and Random Forest diagnostics focused on T2
secondary_changes: rank concordance between the multi-head and Random Forest diagnostics

scoring_time.timestamp_definition: second and later inquiries.inquiry_at before an observed scheduled visit

population.eligibility: T2 scoring snapshots with a complete 30-day future observation window and no already observed scheduled visit.

validation.strategy: same temporal lead-cohort train/validation/test as Modelo 3
validation.split_description: Chronological 70/15/15 split by lead creation with all snapshots from a lead kept in one partition; importance is measured only on T2 test.

items.evidence: Inherited from the leakage-safe Modelo 3 pipeline; lead_score_internal remains blocked.
Only inquiry payload fields known when the inquiry arrives are predictors.
Mutable spot snapshot fields remain excluded.
Compatibility features use only information available at scoring time.
Backward as-of join is inherited from Modelo 3.

items.source: prior inquiries and responses already realized
items.evidence: Historical response features require the response event to have already happened.
Flags describe which point-in-time contexts are available and do not use future outcomes.
